experiment_name: Self-play training-plumbing smoke bit-exact reproducibility check (two independent runs, same seed)

algorithm_config.fix_under_test: scripts/selfplay_train_smoke.py now seeds Python random, NumPy, and torch RNGs (GLOBAL_SEED=42) before MonopolyZeroNet() is constructed, since its value_head is never overwritten by load_ppo_actor and was previously left at an unseeded random init
algorithm_config.game_decision_seed_logic: unchanged (SEEDS 501/502/503 per game, decision_seed derived internally by arena.play_game as before)

result: REPRODUCIBILITY PASSED. Two independent process launches of scripts/selfplay_train_smoke.py, same seed, same clean git HEAD (3b7db1f06bc60ca7f31497034efb42dd705e770e): every deterministic field matched exactly - positions_collected_total (709=709), per-game winners, batch_size_sampled, all four loss/train_step_stats values (bit-identical), and parameters_changed_count (16/16 both runs). Only elapsed_s and peak_rss_gib differed (timing/memory noise, expected). This confirms the RNG-seeding fix (Python/NumPy/torch seeded before MonopolyZeroNet construction) closed the previously-documented non-determinism gap. FixedAdapter.compatibility_fallbacks was read directly this time (0/0/0 for fixed-a/b/c in both runs) instead of left null.
notes: This entry corrects/supersedes the reproducibility caveat in 010-selfplay-training-plumbing-smoke.json's notes field, which reported non-byte-identical results (721 vs 697 positions) between two runs and attributed it to expected self_play=True exploration randomness. That attribution undercounted the actual cause: the model's value_head was also unseeded at construction time. Both are now fixed by explicit RNG seeding; 010's own numbers are left as originally recorded (historical record), not edited.
